page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL4 is a KVM-hypervised virtual server built on the x86_64 CPU architecture. It features 16 shared vCPUs paired with 192.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 12.0 GB per vCPU. The server does not include local storage, meaning storage must be attached externally. It comes with one complimentary public IPv4 address.

The primary differentiator of this instance is its graphics acceleration hardware. It is equipped with two NVIDIA L4 GPUs from the Ada Lovelace architecture family, providing a combined total of 48 GB of VRAM. This hardware configuration is designed to accelerate parallel computing tasks, machine learning workloads, and graphics rendering without relying solely on the shared CPU resources.

Given the shared CPU allocation, this server offers a cost-effective entry point for GPU-heavy workloads that require substantial system memory but do not demand dedicated, constant CPU performance. The high memory capacity of 192.0 GB supports large datasets in memory. This profile is suitable for machine learning inference, medium-scale model training, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated rendering tasks where local storage is not a primary requirement.
